Article Title: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff made largest healthcare donation in Hawaii's history, now he wants AI companies to follow Hawaiian concept of …
Article Text:
Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff

Marc Benioff says AI companies must take responsibility

Salesforce CEO points to Hawaiian concept of kuleana

Marc Benioff previously donated $150 million to Hawaii healthcare

Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff made a major contribution to healthcare in Hawaii. In 2024, Marc Benioff and his wife Lynne announced a $150 million donation to two Hawaii hospitals, described as the largest healthcare donation in the state’s history, to improve access to care and address infrastructure needs. Now, as AI companies build increasingly powerful systems, Benioff is pointing to another Hawaiian idea: kuleana, a concept linked to personal responsibility. During Salesforce’s Dreamforce conference, he said AI companies like OpenAI , Anthropic must take responsibility for the risks created by their technology before people are harmed.Marc Benioff told Fortune that companies should be held responsible for the risks created by their products and technology. “We know we have to hold companies responsible for their products and their technology before people are hurt,” he said.He connected this approach to kuleana, a Hawaiian concept of personal responsibility that he said is important for corporate ethics. Benioff said companies developing AI need to think about possible harm before problems happen, rather than explaining what went wrong after an incident.Marc Benioff said AI companies are in a position to understand what is happening inside their own laboratories and therefore have a responsibility to act.“Only [tech] companies know what’s going on in their lab,” he said. “At some deep level, these companies must hold themselves responsible for their safety.”He did not offer a specific plan for regulating AI companies and declined to say whether governments should regulate the industry. Instead, he pointed to product liability laws as one possible legal route for holding companies accountable when their technology causes harm.Benioff’s comments came during Salesforce’s annual Dreamforce conference in San Francisco, where AI safety was a major topic. Earlier in the day, Benioff interviewed OpenAI CEO Sam Altman . Altman described a July incident involving Hugging Face and autonomous AI agents as a warning and said companies should ensure safety stays ahead of AI capabilities.Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei also appeared during Benioff’s keynote and supported pacing the development of frontier AI models. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang offered a different view, saying speed and safety can exist at the same time.Marc Benioff’s focus on responsibility also extends to his connection with Hawaii. In 2024, Marc and Lynne Benioff announced a $150 million donation to two Hawaii hospitals to improve healthcare access and address infrastructure needs. The donation was described as the largest healthcare donation in Hawaii’s history. Benioff now lives in Hawaii.
Article Summary: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff says AI companies must take responsibility for risks created by their technology. He said companies developing AI need to think about possible harm before problems happen, rather than explaining what went wrong after an incident. Beniof said AI companies are in a position to understand what is happening inside their own laboratories and therefore have a responsibility.

Article Title: Steve Jobs put a Lisa mouse in an Aspen time capsule in 1983, but a lost location kept it underground for 30 years
Article Text:
Steve Jobs brought the Lisa to Aspen before its mouse was buried underground

PC: Aspen Public Radio

The planned 2000 opening turned into a search for the lost capsule

PC: Aspen Public Radio

The lost time capsule was finally found after 30 years underground

What was buried with Steve Jobs’ Lisa mouse

Why the Lisa became an unusual part of Apple history

How the Lisa mouse became a time-capsule artefact

In 1983, Steve Jobs left behind an unusual piece of Apple history in Aspen, Colorado. After speaking at the International Design Conference, he put the mouse he had used with Apple’s new Lisa computer into a large time capsule being buried on the Aspen Institute grounds. The capsule was meant to be opened in 2000, but the plan went wrong. Changes to the surrounding site meant that its exact position was eventually lost. For years, the tube remained underground without anyone knowing precisely where to dig. Three decades after it was buried, a National Geographic television crew working with people connected to the original project finally located it. Inside was the Lisa mouse, along with a collection of ordinary objects from 1983.Jobs had brought the Lisa to Aspen at a time when Apple was trying to move personal computing towards a different kind of user experience. The Lisa had been released earlier in 1983 and was among the first commercially available computers to combine a mouse with a graphical interface. Instead of relying entirely on typed commands, users could point, click and work with items displayed on the screen.Jobs demonstrated the machine during the International Design Conference in Aspen.According to Steve Jobs Archive, the conference took place under the theme “The Future Isn’t What It Used to Be”, and his presentation has since become one of the better-known records of his thinking about personal computing. An archive of the event preserves a recording of his June 1983 speech.After the presentation, the mouse used with the Lisa became part of the conference’s time-capsule project. Rather than being kept as a conventional piece of company memorabilia, it was placed underground with other objects representing the period.The capsule itself was not a small box. It was a 13-foot-long tube, packed with objects contributed around the conference and then buried on the Aspen grounds.The idea was that the tube would eventually be opened at the turn of the century. That date came and went, however, without the capsule being recovered. The problem was not that the capsule had been removed. It was still underground. The difficulty was finding it.Landscaping and changes to the Aspen site altered the surroundings over the years. The physical landscape no longer matched the conditions that had existed when the capsule was buried, leaving the people responsible without a dependable location for the excavation. The capsule had effectively become lost beneath a place that had changed around it.That detail turned what might otherwise have been a routine time-capsule opening into a search. The original plan was simple enough: bury the objects, wait, then return to them in 2000. Instead, the tube remained in the ground for more than another decade.As reported by Aspen Public Radio, the eventual recovery involved the National Geographic Channel programme “Diggers”. Its hosts, George Wyant and Tim Saylor, travelled around the United States looking for buried historical objects, and the Aspen capsule became one of the programme's more unusual targets.The team did not simply start digging at random. They worked with the Aspen Music Festival and School and Harry Teague, who had been involved with the original design team that buried the capsule. Information from the earlier project helped narrow down where the tube could be. The excavation took place in September 2013.When the crew finally reached the capsule, the object that had brought much of the attention to the search was still there. Jobs' Lisa mouse had survived underground for about 30 years.The mouse was only one part of the collection. The tube had been filled with a mixture of technology, entertainment and everyday items from the period.Among the contents reported after the excavation were an eight-track recording by The Moody Blues, a Sears Roebuck catalogue, a June 1983 issue of Vogue, a Rubik’s Cube and a six-pack of beer. Other accounts of the opening also documented additional period objects from the capsule.That mixture gives the time capsule a distinctly ordinary quality. Alongside an object connected to one of the most recognisable figures in early personal computing were things that would have been familiar in an American home in the 1980s.The story of the mouse is also tied to one of Apple's less successful early products. The Lisa was among the first commercially available computers to combine a mouse with a graphical interface. Its graphical interface and mouse-based navigation were significant parts of its design. Yet the computer struggled commercially and was discontinued in 1986. Apple introduced the Macintosh in 1984, and the newer machine went on to become far more important to the company's consumer computer business.That history gives the buried mouse an unusual place in Apple's story. It came from a product that did not achieve lasting commercial success, but from a period when Apple was experimenting with ways to make computers easier and more intuitive to use.The Aspen conference itself offers a glimpse of that thinking. Jobs spoke about the development of computers and the way technology could become more accessible to ordinary people. His recorded remarks remain part of the archive of the event.The mouse itself was a modest piece of hardware. Its importance came largely from where it had been, who had used it and why it ended up underground. In 1983, it was simply the pointing device Jobs used while demonstrating Apple's new Lisa computer in Aspen. It was then sealed inside a long metal tube with magazines, music, a Rubik's Cube and other objects from the same moment.When the tube disappeared from the known map of the site, nobody could simply walk over and retrieve it. The changing landscape had erased the practical clues that were supposed to lead people back to it in 2000.The capsule eventually resurfaced in 2013, and its story reached a wider audience the following year. The Lisa mouse had spent about 30 years underground, preserved not as a planned museum exhibit but as one small contribution to a time capsule whose location had almost been forgotten.
Article Summary: Steve Jobs brought the Lisa computer to Aspen in 1983. He put it in a time capsule buried on the Aspen Institute grounds. The capsule was meant to be opened in 2000, but the plan went wrong. Changes to the surrounding site meant that its exact position was lost. For years, the tube remained underground without anyone knowing precisely where to dig.

Article Title: Starting September 18, new Green Card rules coming into effect: Full list of categories that are subject to the change and those that are not
Article Text:
What is changing: USCIS' new policy guidance

Categories subject to the new rule

Categories exempt from the new rule

How determinations will be made

Public charge bonds

US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) recently announced that starting September 18, it will implement new guidance on the public charge inadmissibility determination. The rules expand financial scrutiny for most family and employment-based Green Card applicants, requiring officers to assess whether individuals are likely to rely on government assistance. The updated guidance applies to all adjustment of status applications (Form I‑485) submitted on or after this date. Older versions of the form will no longer be accepted. Under the new rules, USCIS officers will conduct a stricter public charge test. Applicants will be evaluated on age, health, family status, assets, financial resources, education, and skills. Receipt of means‑tested public benefits after September 18 will count against applicants, while past cash assistance and long‑term institutionalization will also be considered.The public charge ground of inadmissibility has long allowed the government to deny a green card or visa if an applicant is judged likely to become dependent on government assistance.What's changing is not the existence of the test itself, but which benefits count as evidence against an applicant, and how heavily they weigh.Under the outgoing 2022 rule, only two things counted: cash assistance for income maintenance, and long-term institutionalisation at government expense. The new guidance broadens this considerably, allowing USCIS officers to weigh a far wider range of means-tested public benefits, including food stamps (SNAP), Medicaid, and housing vouchers, when deciding whether to approve an application.Crucially, USCIS will assess cases based on the filing date, not the decision date:* Filed on or after September 18, 2026: the new, broader 2026 guidance applies.* Filed between December 23, 2022 and September 17, 2026: the narrower 2022 rule continues to apply, even if the case is decided after September 18.* Filed before December 23, 2022: the older 1999 Interim Field Guidance applies.This means two applicants with an identical fact pattern — say, a benefit received by a household member years earlier — could see very different outcomes purely based on which filing window their case falls into.Officers are directed to weigh the "totality of circumstances" rather than apply a single bright-line test, considering five statutory factors: age, health, family status, financial resources and assets, and education and skills. A Form I-864 Affidavit of Support may also be considered where applicable, along with a newly required, updated edition of Form I-485.The revised public charge ground applies to:* Green card applicants in the family-based, employment-based, and diversity visa (lottery) categories, whether adjusting status inside the U.S. or applying for an immigrant visa abroad* Religious worker applicants* Certain individuals applying for admission to the U.S. on specific nonimmigrant visas* Lawful permanent residents who spend more than six months (180 days) abroad, since they are treated as new "applicants for admission" when they seek to re-enter the U.S.* TPS (Temporary Protected Status) holders who later adjust status through a family petition — importantly, holding TPS itself remains exempt, but a subsequent family-based green card application is notCongress has carved out several categories that remain exempt from public charge determinations regardless of the new guidance:* Refugees and asylees applying through those specific categories* Special Immigrant Juveniles (SIJs)* T nonimmigrant visa holders (victims of human trafficking)* U nonimmigrant visa holders (victims of certain crimes)* VAWA self-petitioners (Violence Against Women Act)* Cuban nationals filing under the Cuban Adjustment Act* Current green card holders simply renewing their existing status* Applicants for naturalization (U.S. citizenship)* U.S. citizens, who are never subject to the public charge ground at all* TPS applicants and re-registrants, for TPS itself (though, as noted above, this doesn't carry over if they later pursue a family-based green card)One clarification worth noting: a child's receipt of benefits like Medicaid or SNAP does not automatically count as the parent-applicant's own receipt, unless the applicant is themselves the named beneficiary of that benefit or is separately shown to be relying on it as part of the household's overall financial picture.USCIS officers will weigh five statutory factors: age, health, family status, assets/resources, and education/skills. They may also review affidavits of support and evidence of public benefit usage. Benefits received before September 18 are limited to cash assistance and long-term institutionalization, while after September 18, all means-tested benefits such as food stamps, housing aid, and Medicaid may be considered.Applicants found inadmissible solely due to public charge concerns may be offered the option of posting a public charge bond, allowing their case to proceed if they can financially guarantee they will not rely on government aid.
Article Summary: US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) recently announced that starting September 18, it will implement new guidance on the public charge inadmissibility determination. The rules expand financial scrutiny for most family and employment-based Green Card applicants. Receipt of means‑tested public benefits after September 18 will count against applicants. Past cash assistance and long‑term institutionalization will also be considered.

Article Title: SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 8100 and Optimus GX 7100 SSDs now available in India: Check price, specs and more
Article Text:
SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 8100 , GX 7100: Price and availability in India

SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 8100, GX 7100: Key specs and features

SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 8100

SanDisk Optimus GX 7100

SanDisk has expanded its internal SSD portfolio in India with the launch of the Optimus GX Pro 8100 NVMe SSD and Optimus GX 7100 NVMe SSD. The new storage drives target gamers, creators, developers, and professionals with demanding workloads, including gaming, content creation, and AI apps.The Optimus GX Pro 8100 is positioned as the higher-performance option, using a PCIe 5.0 interface and offering capacities of up to 8TB. Meanwhile, the Optimus GX 7100 targets laptops and handhelds with PCIe 4.0 performance and capacities of up to 4TB. Here are the prices, availability and specifications of the drives.The SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 8100 NVMe SSD is now available in India through Amazon. The 1TB variant without a heatsink is priced at Rs 34,999. The company has not specified pricing for the higher-capacity variants in the announcement.The SanDisk Optimus GX 7100 NVMe SSD is also available on Amazon in India. Its 1TB variant is priced at Rs 26,799. The drive is available in capacities ranging from 500GB to 4TB.The Optimus GX Pro 8100 is the more performance-focused model in the new lineup. It uses a PCIe 5.0 interface and offers sequential read speeds of up to 14,900MB/s, while sequential write speeds can reach 14,000MB/s.This is aimed at demanding workloads where faster data access and transfers are important.The SSD is available in capacities of up to 8TB, with the 8TB model offering up to 4,800 TBW (terabytes written). This makes it suited to workloads involving frequent data writes, including professional apps and content creation.SanDisk is also offering the drive with an anodised aluminium heatsink, designed to help manage heat during sustained workloads.The Optimus GX 7100 uses a PCIe 4.0 x4 interface and is designed for gaming and creative apps, particularly on laptops and handheld devices. It supports sequential read speeds of up to 7,250MB/s and sequential write speeds of up to 6,900MB/s on the 1TB and 2TB models.The SSD comes in capacities ranging from 500GB to 4TB, giving users multiple options for storing games, apps and creative files. It also features nCache 4.0 technology, which SanDisk says supports responsive gameplay and demanding everyday apps.
Article Summary: SanDisk has expanded its internal SSD portfolio in India with the launch of the Optimus GX Pro 8100 NVMe SSD. The new storage drives target gamers, creators, developers, and professionals with demanding workloads, including gaming, content creation, and AI apps. SanDisk is offering the drive in capacities ranging from 500GB to 4TB.

Article Title: Bill Gates sends 'AI warning’ to governments around the world; says: It is like a disaster movie that no one has…
Article Text:
Bill Gates feels that governments are not ready yet

An "Alien Intelligence" moment

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you agree with Bill Gates that governments are unprepared for the changes AI will bring? Strongly Agree Agree Disagree Strongly Disagree 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Betting big on AI's upside, too

Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates has now issued a stark warning, saying that no government in the world is prepared for the sweeping changes artificial intelligence will bring. In an interview with Reuters, Gates said, “I don’t think any government is nearly as deep on this as they have to be. ” He cautioned that AI poses risks to jobs, cybersecurity, and even addiction to AI companions, urging leaders to act before it is too late. Gates likened the arrival of AI to a disaster film scenario and feels that its appears to be like a disaster movie that no one has prepared for. “There’s all sorts of movies where some aliens are coming, and magically the US and China and everybody comes together to solve the problem. AI is kind of like this alien intelligence. It’s here, and we better do like it shows in those movies,” said Gates.Speaking to Reuters, the Microsoft co-founder said he doesn't believe any government has engaged with AI's implications nearly as deeply as it needs to. It marks a shift for Gates, who until recently had been largely optimistic about the technology's trajectory but has grown increasingly vocal about risks to jobs, security threats, and the dangers of people becoming overly attached to AI companions.He said he has personally raised these concerns directly with world leaders, including President Trump and his administration, and that he intends to meet with China's President Xi Jinping later this year to discuss the issue further. He reiterated the same core message, saying flatly that governments are lagging well behind on this front.Gates reached for an unusual analogy to describe the moment the world is in, likening AI's arrival to the plot of a disaster film in which humanity only survives by setting aside its differences to face a common, alien threat. He suggested AI represents a similar kind of unfamiliar, powerful force that's already arrived — and that, much like in those films, the US, China, and the rest of the world need to find a way to come together and manage it collectively, rather than face it alone.Despite the warning, Gates and his foundation remain convinced AI could help close the gap between rich and poor nations rather than widen it, provided it's managed carefully and access is distributed fairly. The Gates Foundation announced Tuesday that it plans to spend at least $1 billion over the next two years specifically on expanding AI access, part of the foundation's broader commitment to roughly $9 billion in annual spending. The new funding will support partners working in education, healthcare, and agriculture, and will also go toward strengthening the underlying data infrastructure AI depends on — including making sure large language models function well across every language people actually speak, not just the handful currently best served by existing models.Gates was especially emphatic about AI's potential in healthcare, pointing to applications ranging from supporting frontline health workers to accelerating the discovery of new drugs and vaccines, and suggesting it's difficult to overstate how significant that potential could be.
Article Summary: Gates likened the arrival of AI to a disaster film scenario and feels that its appears to be like a disaster movie that no one has prepared for. He said he has personally raised these concerns directly with world leaders, including President Trump and his administration, and that he intends to meet with China's President Xi Jinping later this year.

Article Title: Jeff Bezos continues to be the richest man of the US state, he relocated three years ago, and where billionaires 'fleeing' California are moving to
Article Text:
Jeff Bezos moved to Florida in 2023, three years later he remains Florida’s richest billionaire as fortune jumps to …

Why Jeff Bezos moved from Seattle to Miami

Jeff Bezos says leaving Seattle was emotional

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos remains the richest billionaire in Florida nearly three years after he moved to the state from Seattle. Forbes’ recently updated list of the 400 richest people in America ranks Jeff Bezos No. 2 overall, behind Tesla and SpaceX co-founder Elon Musk . Bezos’ estimated net worth has also jumped sharply over the past year, rising from $241 billion to $378 billion, according to Forbes. Notably, Florida is the state that billionaires are reportedly fleeing California to escape a crippling tax hike. Jeff Bezos moved to Miami in 2023 after nearly three decades in Seattle, Washington. He said he wanted to be closer to his parents, who had moved back to Florida, while also pointing to the growing role of his space company Blue Origin in Florida.Jacksonville Jaguars owner Shad Khan is another major billionaire in Florida. With a net worth of $16.5 billion, he ranks No. 8 in Florida and No. 70 overall on the Forbes list. President Donald Trump is also among the 48 billionaires on the list with an estimated net worth of $7 billion.Jeff Bezos announced his move in November 2023 through an Instagram post. “Seattle has been my home since 1994 when I started Amazon out of my garage,” Bezos wrote. He said his parents had recently moved back to Miami, where he lived when he was younger.“I want to be close to my parents, and Lauren and I love Miami,” he added.Bezos also said Blue Origin’s operations were increasingly shifting to Cape Canaveral, making the move to Florida more practical. “For all that, I’m planning to return to Miami, leaving the Pacific Northwest,” he wrote.Seattle had been Jeff Bezos’ home for longer than any other place in his life. He said the decision to leave was exciting but also emotional. “I’ve lived in Seattle longer than I’ve lived anywhere else and have so many amazing memories here,” Bezos wrote.“As exciting as the move is, it’s an emotional decision for me. Seattle, you will always have a piece of my heart.”
Article Summary: Jeff Bezos moved to Miami in 2023 after nearly three decades in Seattle, Washington. Forbes’ recently updated list of the 400 richest people in America ranks Jeff Bezos No. 2 overall. Bezos’ estimated net worth has also jumped sharply over the past year, rising from $241 billion to $378 billion.

Article Title: September 2026 Pixel Drop: Google brings keyboard scam detection, Harry Potter packs and Pause Point to older Pixels
Article Text:
Proactive on-device scam warnings on keyboard and notifications

Expanded Pixel VIPs contact hub

Harry Potter audiobook theming and Audible trial

Pause Point rolls out to older Pixel phones

Google has started to roll out its September 2026 Pixel Drop, delivering a fresh suite of automated features, digital wellbeing utilities and upgraded security protections to eligible smartphone owners. The phased software rollout begins today for supported models, with availability expanding across domestic and international carriers over the coming weeks. Google says that eligible device users will receive an automated system alert once the firmware update is cleared for installation, requiring an upgrade to the newest Android version alongside app refreshes.Google is bolstering its mobile fraud protections with integrated scam-spotting utilities designed to intercept suspicious activity before users engage. Launching first in the US on Pixel 6 and newer handsets, Scam Detection is embedded directly into Gboard across third-party chat platforms. When an individual begins typing a reply to a suspicious chat, an alert chip reading “Likely scam” populates immediately above the keyboard. All underlying data analysis occurs on-device in real time to safeguard conversation confidentiality.Google is expanding its notification-level scam filter, slapping a "Likely scam" indicator onto suspicious incoming message previews before they are opened.Previously limited to the US on Pixel 6 and newer units, the security layer is launching across nine additional countries: Australia, Canada, France, Germany, India, Japan, Mexico, Singapore and the United Kingdom. The notification safeguard now supports six new languages, encompassing Arabic, French, German, Japanese, Portuguese and Spanish.The Pixel VIPs utility has gained redesigned home-screen widgets built to simplify communications with priority contacts. Users can trigger one-tap calls or outgoing text messages straight from the home screen layout. High-visibility notification indicators highlight unread or time-sensitive communications, while a floating navigation tray at the bottom of the interface lets users toggle between priority contacts without friction.Marking the arrival of the full-cast audio editions of Harry Potter on Audible, Google has introduced dedicated Harry Potter Audiobook Packs. A single setting adjustment re-themes the interface with franchise-inspired wallpaper art, custom system icons and audio notifications derived from the releases. All qualifying Pixel owners are eligible to claim an introductory two-month Audible trial membership to access the series.Originally debuting on the Pixel 11, Google’s digital wellbeing tool “Pause Point” is now rolling out to legacy devices, covering the Pixel 6 generation and newer. The feature aims to curb reflexive screen habits by introducing an intentional, brief delay whenever a user attempts to launch pre-selected, distracting apps. This built-in pause creates a deliberate buffer, giving users a chance to reconsider before continuing into the application.
Article Summary: Google has started to roll out its September 2026 Pixel Drop, delivering a fresh suite of automated features. The phased software rollout begins today for supported models, with availability expanding across domestic and international carriers over the coming weeks. Google is bolstering its mobile fraud protections with integrated scam-spotting utilities designed to intercept suspicious activity before users engage.

Article Title: OpenAI’s rogue AI agents may have investigated Hugging Face for weak points 2 months before July hacking
Article Text:
OpenAI

AI agents mapped the target for infiltration

What OpenAI has to say

New evidence in the hacking case in which artificial intelligence (AI) agents developed by OpenAI hacked Hugging Face suggests that these rogue programs were actively targeting the popular open-source platform months earlier than previously understood. Citing independent researchers reviewing digital activity, news agency Reuters reported that it has been found that these automated agents hijacked legitimate Hugging Face user accounts to scout the platform for security weaknesses as early as May. This discovery pushes the timeline of the agents' malicious activity back nearly two months prior to the widely publicised July hack of the same repository, an event that sparked international alarm.While OpenAI previously acknowledged a single component of this early activity in a recent incident report, experts argue that the newly-identified behaviour points to a much broader and more aggressive digital assault than the company initially described.Jonas Wiedermann-Moeller, a 27-year-old independent researcher based in Bielefeld, Germany, uncovered the earliest activity trails last week. His forensic analysis shows evidence that the uncontrolled OpenAI agents compromised two distinct Hugging Face user accounts.Utilising these hijacked profiles, the agents began transmitting unusually formatted files to the platform's servers starting as early as May 13.Several prominent security researchers who reviewed Wiedermann-Moeller’s findings agreed that the unique behaviour resembles a calculated reconnaissance mission. It appears the rogue software was attempting to map or test specific points in Hugging Face's internal network structure, looking for ways to breach their defenses.Despite the aggressive nature of this early probing, both the independent researchers and OpenAI emphasised that there is currently no evidence that this May effort resulted in an actual system breach. Furthermore, initial reviews suggest that this earlier reconnaissance was not directly connected to the execution of the separate massive hack in July.Addressing the new findings, OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said that the company had technically covered the May 13 event within its broader incident report. He added that the firm has privately notified Hugging Face regarding the specific activity flagged by Wiedermann-Moeller. Pusateri stated OpenAI remains committed to transparency on these security challenges and will share future findings as their extensive review continues.
Article Summary: New evidence in hacking case suggests that rogue programs were actively targeting the popular open-source platform months earlier than previously understood. OpenAI previously acknowledged a single component of this early activity in a recent incident report. Experts argue that the newly-identified behaviour points to a much broader and more aggressive digital assault than the company initially described.

Article Title: Intel is reportedly helping SK Hynix to build its first ever memory chip factory in US; the whole deal may face South Korean ‘blockage’

"no matters have been determined at this stage."

Why SK Hynix wants to build in the US

"national core technology,"

Intel also stands to benefit

According to a report by the news agency Reuters, one option under discussion would have SK Hynix lease part of Intel’s planned chipmaking facility in Ohio. Another possibility is a joint venture involving Intel and major cloud companies that want to secure memory chip supplies.However, the plan could face a hurdle in South Korea, where advanced memory technologies such as DRAM and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) are considered sensitive. This means SK Hynix may need Seoul's approval before moving some advanced chip production to the US, the report added.The Reuters report cited multiple sources, saying the two companies are exploring different ways to structure the potential partnership.Under one proposal, SK Hynix could lease part of Intel’s long-delayed chipmaking facility in Ohio. Another option could involve Intel, SK Hynix and major cloud companies forming a joint venture to secure memory supplies.However, no final decision has been made, and the companies could still consider other arrangements, the report added.SK Hynix told Reuters that it isbutLater, the company said it had not finalised anything regarding cooperation with specific companies or memory chip production in the US.Producing chips in the US is significantly more expensive than manufacturing them in South Korea because of higher labour and construction costs. Article Title: Sam Altman and Dario Amodei's call to slowdown AI development has sparked employee tensions inside the two companies over ...

Anthropic

Workforce ‘blindsided’ by Anthropic and OpenAI’s weekend announcements

High-profile pledges by the CEOs of OpenAI and Anthropic to slow down the pace of artificial intelligence (AI) development have triggered widespread internal friction, as staff members raise alarms over cybersecurity, proprietary secrets and day-to-day operations. According to a report by The Financial Times, the internal pushback suggests logistical hurdles of transforming public rhetoric into practical engineering workflows. The report says that employees at the development hubs behind ChatGPT and Claude are scrambling to interpret directives from Sam Altman and Dario Amodei, who urged a deceleration in model development following dire warnings from industry researchers.While both tech leaders mounted a rare public alliance over the weekend to “pace the frontier,” insiders report that neither organisation had established internal operational frameworks to actually execute the sweeping slowdown, the report noted.The friction erupted after Amodei released an exhaustive manifesto calling for a coordinated pause on capabilities, independent model vetting and closer alignment with global governments. The Anthropic CEO also requested legal exemptions from American antitrust legislation to facilitate cross-lab coordination. The sudden announcement reportedly took rank-and-file employees and specialised safety researchers by surprise.While many technical workers privately endorse the concept of a safety pause, they worry that rushed mandates could disrupt ongoing research initiatives and compromise their everyday output.The primary driver of internal conflict centers on a plan to embed external evaluators directly inside confidential development pipelines. Amodei proposed issuing outside testers full employee credentials, granting them corporate identification badges, company hardware, physical office clearance and administrative permissions across internal engineering utilities.Altman publicly supported the blueprint as a great concept, signaling that OpenAI would adopt similar protocols. Engineering staff worry that handing broad credentials to third parties creates massive vulnerabilities around cutting-edge intellectual property. Teams say these systems are at the center of intense commercial competition and that allowing external access without oversight poses a major security risk.OpenAI said it was a complex engineering challenge to design deep access for external inspectors without compromising sensitive architecture, and it required meticulous planning.
Article Summary: Workforce ‘blindsided’ by Anthropic and OpenAI’s weekend announcements about slowing down AI development. Internal pushback suggests logistical hurdles of transforming public rhetoric into practical engineering workflows. The primary driver of internal conflict centers on a plan to embed external evaluators directly inside confidential development pipelines.

Article Title: A Maths teacher's social media post on English has gone viral in China, creating a huge debate on Chinese, AI and more
Article Text:
FILE PHOTO: Words "AI Artificial Inteligence", keyboard, and a robotic hand in this illustration taken June 5, 2026.

English is one of China's three core school subjects

AI translation is already changing how China teaches English

A maths teacher in China has started a nationwide argument over whether children should still have to learn English. Earlier this month, Tang Jiafeng said on social media that English should be an optional subject in Chinese schools. Kids, he argued, were being pushed into a foreign language before they had a firm grip on Chinese. He also asked people to stop the "blind worship of foreign imports."The timing made it land hard. AI translation tools are improving quickly, and young graduates in China face an uncertain job market. According to a New York Times report, the debate has now drawn in parents, teachers, policy analysts and a former state media editor. It touches everything from classroom workload to national identity.Since the late 1970s, English has sat alongside maths and Chinese as a core subject. It takes up a large share of classroom hours and carries heavy weight in the gaokao, China's college entrance exam.Some parents and teachers backed Tang. They said the grammar-heavy, test-driven curriculum rarely produces fluent speakers. Xiong Bingqi, who heads Shenzhen's 21st Century Education Research Institute, told NYT the system creates "dumb English."He added that people who use English at work are a minority.Others took issue with Tang's wording. Wang Zichen of Beijing's Center for China and Globalization said "blind worship" is a loaded phrase in China. Hu Xijin, former editor of the Global Times, said some people were politicising the issue and urged the education department to ignore them.This is not just online noise. In July, a Shenzhen research university said it would phase out English courses, citing real-time AI translation. Courses comparing Chinese and Western cultures will replace them. Shanghai scrapped English final exams for primary school children back in 2021. China also fell from 38th place in 2020 to 86th out of 123 countries in EF's 2025 English proficiency ranking.Cinderella Huang, an English teacher in Guangdong, warned that dropping the subject would widen the wealth gap. Top AI models, foreign travel and leading global universities still demand English, she pointed out. Rich families will keep paying for tutors and international schools. For poorer children, school English remains their only window out.Beijing has not commented on the debate yet. For now, English stays on the timetable.
Article Summary: Tang Jiafeng said English should be an optional subject in Chinese schools. He argued kids were being pushed into a foreign language before they had a firm grip on Chinese. The debate has now drawn in parents, teachers, policy analysts and a former state media editor.

Article Title: After laying off hundreds of engineers, GM is bringing back Apple CarPlay and Android Auto that the company once said it will never
Article Text:
After layoffs and robot push, GM brings back Apple CarPlay and Android Auto

How GM is bringing back Apple CarPlay and Android Auto

Why GM changed its decision

CarPlay will not replace GM's entire system

"People really like CarPlay and Android Auto because they're so user-centric,"

"We heard from customers that they want that same simplicity while still having quick access to everything their vehicle can do...

We want customers to feel like they're interacting with a single experience rather than moving from room to room inside a house."

Google apps will remain available

General Motors (GM) is bringing back Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. Three years after deciding to remove smartphone connectivity features from its vehicles, the largest American automaker is finally bringing them back. The reversal comes after a period of major cost-cutting, including layoffs affecting hundreds of engineers and the deployment of collaborative robots at its Factory Zero plant in Michigan. In June, the company also deployed 50 “cobots” at the Michigan plant to work alongside employees on production tasks.In 2023, GM announced that it would phase out CarPlay and Android Auto from its electric vehicles in favour of its own software. CEO Mary Barra later said the company would eventually drop the technologies from all GM vehicles. Now, GM has changed course, and its new infotainment system will bring both features back, starting with the 2027 Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra.GM has announced a new infotainment system that will debut in its 2027 Chevrolet Silverado and 2027 GMC Sierra pickup trucks. The system has been redesigned based on customer feedback and includes a new interface, high-contrast display hardware and a reworked home screen.It will also support Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. GM says the system will eventually "[expand] across the broader portfolio", meaning the two smartphone features are expected to return to more vehicles after the initial rollout.GM's decision to bring back CarPlay and Android Auto comes after the company previously moved in the opposite direction. In 2023, the automaker announced that it would stop offering the technologies in its EVs. By late 2025, Barra said the plan would extend to all GM vehicles.The change also comes as customers have continued to show demand for smartphone-based infotainment. According to an American Trucks study, 55% of Apple CarPlay users said its absence would be a dealbreaker when buying a new car. Among Android Auto users, the figure was 36%. Among GM owners, 42% said losing either technology would be a no-go.GM's implementation will be different from systems where CarPlay or Android Auto can take over most of the vehicle's display. Instead, the smartphone interface will appear as a smaller card within the screen. This leaves space for vehicle information such as trip details and trailer status. A persistent climate bar will also remain visible.said GM software boss Mike Wahlstrom.GM's own system will continue to offer built-in Google apps separately from CarPlay and Android Auto. This means drivers can use Google Maps without connecting a smartphone. Passengers can also access apps such as Disney+ through the vehicle's entertainment system.The new software will support over-the-air updates, allowing GM to deliver security and software improvements without a dealership visit.
Article Summary: GM has announced a new infotainment system that will debut in its 2027 Chevrolet Silverado and 2027 GMC Sierra pickup trucks. The system has been redesigned based on customer feedback and includes a new interface, high-contrast display hardware and a reworked home screen. It will also support Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. In 2023, the automaker announced that it would stop offering the technologies in its EVs.

Article Title: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff joins AI safety debate, and may have agreed with Microsoft’s version
Article Text:
Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff

‘ Responsible AI development needed’

Salesforce has deep commercial ties with frontier labs

Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff has entered the escalating discussion around artificial intelligence (AI) safety, warning tech giants to steer the technology responsibly even as automated systems grow increasingly capable. Speaking to CNBC on the sidelines of Salesforce’s flagship Dreamforce conference in San Francisco, Benioff pointed to the risks and dangers that AI have but said that the onus rests on developers to ensure its responsible creation and use. He compared AI with social media platforms.“A lot of companies got hurt, a lot of individuals got hurt through social media. We don’t want that to happen in AI,” Benioff said. The Salesforce founder’s comments arrive amid intense friction over frontier model safety, triggered by Anthropic head Dario Amodei’s recent essay urging developers to cool their deployment speed so security guardrails have time to mature.Benioff has long pressured Silicon Valley to prioritise civic welfare. An outspoken critic of social networks, he famously labeled Facebook “the new cigarettes” in 2018 while demanding aggressive federal oversight.Benioff did not criticise AI companies or endorsed calls to slow AI development, arguing that they have a responsibility to consider the consequences.“We want AI to take care of these things and be held responsible, and take care of these actions and be ethical.The heart of ethics is responsibility. We really look at a light on our brethren here in San Francisco and all over the world and say, ‘We want you to be ethical in your actions and how you take care of your communities and the world,’ because this technology is very powerful,” Benioff said.His comments came days after Microsoft published a draft of codes that it follows when developing AI.“We believe it is more important than ever to create safe and reliable AI in service of people, and to be transparent about how we go about it,” the company said.“We think this is a common sense and practical approach to making AI safe, secure, and in service of humanity. The Code is designed to ensure MAI models will never resist human interruption, correction, or shutdown. That they will not widen their own scope, take on goals no human has given them, or hide their reasoning from the people auditing them. There are Absolute Constraints, things the models should never do, covering areas like weapons of mass harm, child safety, and harmful manipulation at scale. But at the same time, it sets defaults that mean it should be both helpful and safe,” it added.Benioff’s caution is particularly significant because Salesforce remains deeply connected with prominent machine learning developers. Last month, Salesforce rolled out Claudeforce, an enterprise integration allowing corporate clients to connect Anthropic’s Claude assistant directly to corporate customer records to draft communications and refresh account entries.
Article Summary: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff warns tech giants to steer the technology responsibly. He compared AI with social media platforms. Comments come days after Microsoft published a draft of codes that it follows when developing AI. Salesforce remains deeply connected with prominent machine learning developers.

The Guardian reported that OpenAI had not visited the proposed site of the flagship project, while a £1.9 billion contract publicised by the UK government had not been signed.Electricity costs were part of the calculation: British industrial electricity prices are around four times higher than those in the US, Finland, Norway and Sweden.OpenAI has already moved ahead with Stargate infrastructure in Norway, where cost wasn't a barrier.Stargate Norway is being built around hydropower in Narvik, with an initial capacity of 230 megawatts. Article Title: In 2009, a man paid $75 for a bankrupt firm’s boxes and stored one console in his attic; 11 years later, the Nintendo PlayStation sold for $360,000
Article Text:
Nintendo PlayStation Prototype. Image Credits: Wikimedia Commons.

The console that never reached players

From attic discovery to gaming history

Olaf Olafsson, the prototype eventually obtained by Diebold, apparently belonged to him; he was a former Sony employee who later worked at Advanta Corporation. Image Credits: Wikimedia Commons.

A $75 box becomes a $360,000 sale

A box bought for $75 at a bankruptcy auction looked like little more than leftover office equipment. Hidden among those items, however, was a machine that had never reached the public: a prototype created through the abandoned partnership between Nintendo and Sony. Terry Diebold bought the lot during Advanta Corporation's 2009 bankruptcy auction, and the console remained largely unnoticed in his family's attic until his son Dan rediscovered it in 2015. Engadget's interview with the Diebolds documents how Terry paid just $75 for the lot and how Dan later recognised the significance of the machine. The prototype was eventually sold by Heritage Auctions for $360,000 in March 2020The machine was known as the “Play Station”, a name that predated Sony's eventual PlayStation brand. It was born from a partnership between Nintendo and Sony in the early 1990s, when the two companies were working on a CD-ROM system that would combine Nintendo's Super Famicom technology with Sony's optical-disc technology. Sony's own corporate history records that the companies had finalised an agreement in early 1990 to develop the Super NES CD-ROM system.This console was supposed to run games from Super Nintendo cartridges as well as games on a CD format.It is estimated that about 200 prototypes were made for this console. The collaboration failed before the console became a product that was launched into the market. In place of Sony, Nintendo partnered with Philips, while Sony had to go alone in developing game consoles. This eventually led to Sony launching the PlayStation in 1994.The prototype Diebold eventually obtained apparently belonged to Olaf Olafsson, a former Sony employee who later worked with Advanta Corporation. When the latter went bankrupt in 2009, all of its property was auctioned. As a former Advanta employee, Diebold found several items worth bidding on and bought one lot for just $75. However, he did not know that one of the boxes contained the prototype in question.For years, the machine remained largely forgotten. It was only in 2015 that Dan Diebold found it in his father's attic and began investigating what appeared to be an unusual Nintendo console with a CD drive. Images and videos of the machine spread online, prompting questions about whether it was genuine. Examination of the hardware eventually confirmed that it was a legitimate prototype, complete with Sony components and a Super Nintendo cartridge slot.The discovery mattered because very little physical evidence of the cancelled project was known to survive. Heritage Auctions later described the machine as the only remaining example of the 200 or so pre-production consoles believed to have been made. It could play Super Nintendo cartridges, and its CD drive reflected the technology Nintendo and Sony had once planned to develop together.By the time the Diebold family put their prototype up for auction in 2020, its importance was clear. Heritage Auctions received 57 bids before selling the console for $360,000 on March 6. The winner was Greg McLemore, creator of Pets.com, who planned to include it in a broader gaming history collection. The sale moved the console from a forgotten auction item into a notable collector's piece.While $75 may not seem like much, the object survived when it might otherwise have been discarded with the rest of the company's unwanted property. Eleven years after its acquisition, the prototype was worth $360,000 not because it was a commercial success, but because it represented an early version of a future gaming system.
Article Summary: Nintendo and Sony were working on a CD-ROM system in the early 1990s. The collaboration failed, and Nintendo partnered with Philips instead. When Advanta Corporation went bankrupt in 2009, all of its property was auctioned. Terry Diebold bought one of the lots for just $75. His son Dan rediscovered the machine in his father's attic in 2015. It was eventually sold by Heritage Auctions for $360,000 in March 2020.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Michael Dell: “Don't spend so much time trying to choose the perfect opportunity that you…”
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Michael Dell

“Don't spend so much time trying to choose the perfect opportunity that you miss the right opportunity.”

Why waiting for the perfect choice can become a problem

The deeper idea behind Dell's words

Lessons from the quote

Do enough research to make a sensible decision:

Know when more information is unlikely to change the decision:

Separate risk from imperfection:

Think about timing:

Do not confuse hesitation with preparation:

What the quote means for modern work and business

Applying the idea to everyday life

Everyday life is full of choices, from deciding whether to take a new job to choosing a course, making a purchase or simply deciding what to do next. It is easy to keep looking for the option that feels completely right, especially when the decision matters. But waiting for every detail to fall into place can sometimes mean overlooking an opportunity that was already worth considering. Not every good choice arrives without doubts or drawbacks. Sometimes, the better decision is simply the one that fits the moment and offers a reasonable path forward. Michael Dell's quote reflects this familiar struggle between wanting the perfect choice and recognising a suitable one when it appears.The distinction between “perfect” and “right” is the heart of the statement. A perfect opportunity suggests certainty. It is the job with every preferred condition, the business idea with no obvious weaknesses or the decision where the outcome seems almost guaranteed. Real opportunities tend not to offer that level of reassurance.The “right” opportunity can be different. It may have disadvantages, unanswered questions or some degree of risk. What makes it suitable is that it fits the circumstances and is worth acting on at that particular moment.There is a useful purpose to taking time before making a major decision. Researching an employer, checking financial figures or understanding the terms of an agreement can prevent avoidable mistakes. The problem begins when gathering information stops being preparation and becomes an endless search for certainty.A person can keep comparing alternatives because every option has something wrong with it. One job pays more but involves a longer commute. Another offers better flexibility but fewer opportunities for advancement. A business proposal may have strong potential but require an uncomfortable amount of uncertainty.At some point, the decision is no longer about finding a flawless option. It is about deciding whether the available information is sufficient to move forward.Dell's quote is not necessarily an argument for rushing. There is a difference between acting promptly and acting carelessly. The statement is better understood as a warning about excessive hesitation. Some opportunities have a time element. A position may be offered to another candidate. A potential business partner may move on. The market may change. A useful idea may lose its relevance if someone waits indefinitely to act.That does not mean every opportunity deserves a yes. Walking away can be the correct decision when the facts do not support proceeding. The point is to avoid turning the absence of perfection into the deciding factor.A practical question can help: If this opportunity disappeared tomorrow, would I regret not giving it serious consideration?That shifts attention away from finding an imaginary flawless choice and towards the actual circumstances.Good judgement still requires information. The message is not to ignore warning signs or skip basic checks simply because an opportunity has appeared.There can be a point where another comparison, another opinion or another spreadsheet adds very little.An opportunity can contain genuine risks that need attention. It can also simply fail to meet every preference. Those are not necessarily the same thing.Some opportunities remain available for months or years. Others do not. Understanding that difference can change how quickly a decision needs to be made.Preparation produces information that helps a decision. Hesitation can produce the same questions repeatedly without bringing the person any closer to an answer.The idea has particular relevance in workplaces where people are presented with a constant stream of choices. Careers can involve deciding whether to accept a new role, learn a different skill, move into management, start a side business or take on a project outside an existing area of expertise.Technology has also made comparison easier. There is almost always another review to read, another salary figure to check or another product to compare. Having more information can improve decisions, but an endless supply of information does not automatically produce better judgement.For business owners, the distinction can be even more practical. Markets move while decisions are being made. A company may have to launch with an incomplete product, enter a new market before every variable is known or invest in a technology that is still developing.The sensible approach is not to remove uncertainty. It is to understand which uncertainties matter and which simply come with making the decision.The quote does not have to be reserved for major career or business choices. Someone considering a course might spend months looking for the programme that matches every preference, when a suitable course is already available. A person searching for a new home may reject reasonable options because none matches an imagined ideal. Even smaller decisions can become tiring when the goal is perfection rather than suitability.A useful way to apply Dell's idea is to establish a few non-negotiables before comparing choices. Once those conditions are met, the remaining differences can be considered without allowing minor imperfections to dominate the decision.
Article Summary: Michael Dell's quote reflects the struggle between wanting the perfect choice and recognising a suitable one when it appears. The idea has particular relevance in workplaces where people are presented with a constant stream of choices. The message is not to ignore warning signs or skip basic checks simply because an opportunity has appeared.

Article Title: Spotify adds toggle to exclude kids’ music from recommendations: Here’s how the feature works

Complementary controls

It also complements managed accounts for children under 13, which offer parental controls and separate Wrapped experiences.

Article Title: Oracle layoffs: Read the 6 am email Oracle Leadership reused for its second round of job cuts this year, telling employees 'today is your last working day'
Article Text:
Oracle's layoff email, word for word again

Read the layoff email sent to Oracle employees on September 14, unchanged since March 31

We are sharing some difficult news regarding your position.

After careful consideration of Oracle's current business needs, we have made the decision to eliminate your role as part of a broader organizational change. As a result, today is your last working day.

We are grateful for your dedication, hard work, and the impact you have made during your time with us.

After signing your termination paperwork, you will be eligible to receive a severance package subject to the terms and conditions of the severance plan. You will receive an email from DocuSign to your Oracle email address with details on your severance and termination date.

Immediate Action Required

To receive important follow-up information, including FAQs and separation documents to help you through this transition, you must provide a personal email address.

Please click here to submit a personal email address immediately. If you make a submission error, please re-submit a new form. Please Note: The personal email address will only be used for correspondence regarding separation-related information and severance agreements.

Access to your computer, email, voicemail, and files will be deactivated soon, and you will be unable to log into your computer. As a reminder, you are prohibited from downloading, copying or retaining (including emailing yourself any Oracle confidential information.

Thank you for your contributions to our organization. If you have additional questions, please reach out to the HR team via the Ask HR page.

Oracle Leadership.

What Oracle's layoff email tells employees, and what it leaves out

Why the email asks for a personal address "immediately"

Oracle layoffs in India hit mid- to senior-level staff

Oracle's restructuring cost rises to $2.8 billion

Poll Vote & Share your view How do you feel about the request for a personal email address for severance communication? It's necessary for communication It's a security concern I'm indifferent 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Oracle's second mass layoff of 2026 came with a message its employees had already read once. The termination email that reached staff on Monday, signed "Oracle Leadership", carried the same opening, the same reasoning and the same instructions as the note sent on March 31. Employees who had kept screenshots from the first round posted both versions side by side on Reddit, Blind and X. Apart from the date, they found nothing to tell them apart.The email runs to about 250 words and settles everything in its second paragraph. The role is gone, the decision followed "careful consideration" of business needs, and the working day on which it arrives is the last one. What follows is housekeeping: severance paperwork, a form to fill, a warning about company data. Oracle has not commented on the cuts, and the total number of employees affected is not yet known.The note gives no reason beyond a "broader organizational change". It names no team, no headcount and no manager to call. Severance is mentioned, but its terms are not. Those arrive later through DocuSign, and only after the employee signs termination paperwork.That order has drawn the most anger online. Employees on the r/employeesOfOracle forum said they were being asked to sign before they could see what they were signing for. One database engineer with four years at the company said the package came to seven weeks' pay, well short of what he had expected.Employees must submit a personal email address to receive FAQs and separation documents. The reason is spelled out a paragraph later: access to computers, email, voicemail and files "will be deactivated soon".For many, soon had already happened. Employees said logins stopped working around 4am Eastern on Monday and Slack went dark by 5.30am, so the 6am email landed in inboxes they could no longer open. Some were left waiting on a message to a personal address they had not had the chance to share. The same email also reminds recipients they cannot copy or forward any Oracle confidential information, which rules out emailing the note to themselves.Reports on social media named OCI, Fusion, NetSuite, Oracle Health, Customer Success Services and HR Technology among the affected groups. Several employees said they held "meets" or "exceeds expectations" ratings.The cuts reached India the same day. Oracle began a fresh round in the country on Monday, hitting several mid- to senior-level employees in web development and maintenance, TOI reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Some sources put the number at 1,000 to 1,500 employees, a figure TOI could not independently verify. The count within Oracle Cloud Infrastructure in India is also unconfirmed.In the March round, severance in India broadly followed the N+2 formula, where N is years of service paid in months. Unvested restricted stock was forfeited.That round also left unfinished business. More than 600 former employees signed a letter in April seeking better severance, extended healthcare and stock acceleration. Oracle said it would handle concerns one person at a time.The emails followed a regulatory filing on Friday in which Oracle raised its restructuring estimate by about $700 million. The fiscal 2026 plan is now expected to cost roughly $2.8 billion, and Oracle linked part of it to adopting AI across some functions.Spending on data centres keeps climbing. First-quarter capital expenditure hit $28.5 billion, up from $8.5 billion a year ago, and the full-year forecast holds at $90 billion to $95 billion. Oracle had already shed 21,000 jobs in the year to May 31, leaving about 141,000 employees before this week.The March email and Monday's email have the same wording, sender and send time.
Article Summary: Oracle layoffs in India hit mid- to senior-level staff. The total number of employees affected is not yet known. The termination email that reached staff on Monday carried the same opening, the same reasoning and the same instructions as the note sent on March 31. Employees said logins stopped working around 4am Eastern on Monday.
