Article Title: Person-to-merchant UPI payments over Rs 2,000 to attract MDR : What remains free, what will come under MDR and other things to know
Article Text:
MDR on Person-to-merchant UPI payments above Rs 2,000: What will remain free

MDR on Person-to-merchant UPI payments above Rs 2,000: What will attract MDR

MDR on Person-to-merchant UPI payments above Rs 2,000: Customers will not pay MDR

MDR on Person-to-merchant UPI payments above Rs 2,000: Most merchant transactions will remain unaffected

When do the updated MDR provisions take effect

Will small-value UPI transactions be impacted

Will UPI apps start charging platform fee on UPI payments

Will I need to pay a fee when scanning a QR code at a local vendor

Do small merchants need to upgrade or change their existing QR codes

What happens if a small merchant receives a payment above Rs 2,000

UPI AutoPay: No prescribed MDR charges

The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has introduced a 0.4% fee on person-to-merchant transactions exceeding Rs 2,000. Called Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), it is a charge that a merchant pays to a bank or payment service provider for processing a digital payment. Introduced under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, the new MDR provision will come into effect from October 15, 2026. In an official press release, the government clarified that the new UPI framework will have “no impact on any person to person transactions”. “UPI will continue to remain completely free for all person-to-person transactions, irrespective of the amount transferred,” the release said. Instead, “the framework seeks to ensure the long-term sustainability of UPI while protecting individuals and small merchants from additional charges,” it stated.With the new framework coming into force next month, here’s what the government said about what UPI payments remain free, what has been included under the MDR provisions and whether UPI apps will start charging platform fees on UPI payments.All Person-to-Person Transactions: All person-to-person (P2P) UPI transactions will remain completely free, irrespective of the amount transferred.No transaction fee, platform fee or other charge may be imposed on individuals for sending or receiving money through UPI. Therefore, UPI transactions accounting for 70% of the total transaction value will remain completely outside the MDR framework.Merchant Payments Up to Rs 2,000: All person-to-merchant (P2M) transactions up to Rs 2,000 will remain free of MDR. Customers will not be required to pay any charge when making such payments through UPI.Payments Received by Small Merchants: Small merchants including street vendors receiving up to Rs 1 lakh per month through UPI QR codes under the Person-to-Person-Merchant (P2PM) category will continue to enjoy zero MDR on all transactions. This provision will protect street vendors, neighbourhood shops and other small businesses from additional payment costs.Merchant Transactions Above Rs 2,000: A nominal MDR of 0.4% will apply only to P2M transactions above Rs 2,000. The MDR will be shared among payment ecosystem participants, including banks, payment service providers and UPI application providers. For transactions of Rs 75,000 and above, the MDR will be capped at Rs 300 per transaction.Transactions in Essential Sectors: Transactions above Rs 2,000 in essential and thin-margin sectors, including railways, telecommunications, insurance, fuel and agricultural inputs, will attract a flat MDR of Rs 5 per transaction. The flat charge will provide cost certainty for critical public services and businesses operating on narrow margins.Capital Market Transactions: Payments relating to mutual funds, securities, stockbrokers and dealers will attract an MDR of 0.02%, capped at Rs 300 per transaction. The lower rate is intended to support continued retail participation in formal financial markets.MDR is a charge within the merchant payment ecosystem. It is not a charge on customers making UPI payments. In its official announcement, the government said that banks have been advised to ensure that merchants do not pass MDR charges on to customers. UPI application providers are expressly prohibited from imposing platform fees or hidden charges.Individuals will continue to have unlimited free usage, with no monthly quotas, volume restrictions or tiered caps on free UPI transactions. Daily transaction limits prescribed by banks and NPCI, generally ranging from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 5 lakh depending on the transaction category, are security and risk-management safeguards. They are not charging thresholds.Data analysis indicates that MDR will apply to only about 4% of merchant transactions. This means that approximately 96% of merchant transactions will remain unaffected, as they are either below the Rs 2,000 threshold or covered by the zero-MDR framework for small merchants.The framework therefore protects individuals, micro-enterprises and small businesses while introducing a limited charge on larger merchant transactions.The finalized MDR framework and threshold structure take effect from 15th October 2026. This timeline gives acquiring banks, payment aggregators, fintech applications, and corporate accounting platforms adequate lead time to update their software engines and billing systems.There is no impact on small-value UPI transactions up to Rs 2,000, which comprise more than 95% of the total volume of UPI (P2M) transactions. The intent of levying reasonable MDR is to ensure that UPI remains, accessible and convenient for everyday transactions while supporting long-term ecosystem sustainability.No, UPI App providers shall NOT charge Platform Fee or any other charge for any payment made through UPI. UPI applications are explicitly restricted from levying platform fees on UPI transactions.No, scanning QR codes at local markets, street vendors, or small retail shops will remain completely free for consumers. The customer-facing side of a QR transaction involves zero fees, regardless of the purchase amount. The policy has been engineered to protect daily micro-purchases like tea stalls, and local transport from any cost burden. Consumers can continue scanning QR codes with total confidence that no extra charge will be deducted.No. Existing QR infrastructure will continue to function normally. Merchants do not need to replace, re-register, or alter their existing physical QR stands or soundboxes. All UPI QR codes currently displayed across shops will continue to process payments without interruption. Merchants can receive customer payments through their existing setups without visiting a bank branch or updating software.MDR applicability is determined by overall merchant account categorisation. Receiving a payment above Rs 2,000 does not impose a charge on a small merchant operating under exempted tiers like P2PM. A MDR of 0.4% will be introduced on Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000/-. For transactions of Rs 75,000/- and above, the MDR will be capped at Rs 300 per transaction.The government says that recurring payments made through UPI Mandates or AutoPay—such as utility bills, OTT subscriptions and mutual fund subscriptions—do not carry prescribed MDR transaction charges. Hence, they will continue to remain free of any fees.
Article Summary: The National Payments Corporation of India has introduced a 0.4% fee on person- to-merchant transactions exceeding Rs 2,000. Called Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), it is a charge that a merchant pays to a bank or payment service provider for processing a digital payment. The new MDR provision will come into effect from October 15, 2026.

Article Title: Meta’s ‘spy glasses’ may get a camera-free version soon: Report
Article Text:
Meta’s ‘spy glasses’ may get a camera-free version soon

Why Meta glasses are facing privacy concerns

Luna could focus on Meta AI instead of recording

Meta has already tried to stop hidden recording

Developers are building tools to detect smart glasses

Meta expands its AI subscription business

Meta is reportedly working on a new pair of smart glasses without a camera, a major change from its existing Ray-Ban Meta lineup. The reported move comes as camera-equipped smart glasses face growing privacy concerns and bans in places such as schools and cinemas. The new glasses, reportedly codenamed “Luna,” are expected to focus on voice-based AI instead of photo and video recording. According to The Information, Meta could unveil the glasses at its developer conference on September 23-24, with shipments expected to begin in October.As per the report, Luna will have six built-in microphones and a side button that can give users quick access to Meta AI. The glasses are also expected to support Meta's new consumer AI agent, Muse. The speakers are reportedly similar to those used in Meta's current smart glasses.The reported camera-free glasses come as Meta smart glasses face growing privacy concerns. A BBC investigation in January this year identified dozens of accounts that had posted videos of women recorded in public without their consent using Meta glasses. One such video showed the face and phone number of a 21-year-old woman and received more than 1.3 million views.The concerns have also spread to public places. Schools, cinemas and other venues have increasingly banned smart glasses because of the possibility of people being recorded without their knowledge.The reported Luna design suggests Meta may be trying a different approach to AI glasses. The six microphones could make voice interaction the main way users communicate with Meta AI and Muse. The absence of a camera could also make the glasses more acceptable in places where recording devices are not allowed.Meta's existing Ray-Ban Meta glasses have reportedly sold around 7 million units, showing strong interest in AI-powered wearable devices. The challenge for Luna will be whether consumers find voice-based AI useful enough without the camera features that helped make smart glasses attractive.Meta announced a software update in July 2026 aimed at detecting when the recording LED has been “physically tampered with or destroyed.” The company said it would block camera recording when such tampering is detected.Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth has also said the recording light was designed so that people nearby could notice when the camera is being used. However, the privacy debate has continued as more people use camera-equipped smart glasses.Privacy concerns have also led to independent tools designed to identify nearby smart glasses. One example is ZuckOff, a free mobile app developed by Polish developer Pawel Szydlowski. The app uses Bluetooth signals to identify smart glasses that may be nearby.The app can recognise signals associated with devices including Ray-Ban Meta, Oakley Meta and Snap Spectacles. It can provide an approximate idea of how close a pair of glasses is, although it cannot tell whether the glasses are actively recording or identify the person wearing them.The reported Luna launch comes as Meta expands its paid AI services. On September 15, Meta announced Meta One, a subscription service offering additional AI features across Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp. The company said the service has already reached 15 million subscriptions and trials during its phased rollout. Meta plans to expand the service to Edits and AI glasses.
Article Summary: New glasses, reportedly codenamed ‘Luna,’ are expected to focus on voice-based AI instead of photo and video recording. The glasses are also expected to support Meta's new consumer AI agent, Muse. The reported Luna launch comes as Meta expands its paid AI services.

Article Title: Bill Gates announces $1 billion donation to AI efforts after warning that this technology poses grave threat to jobs and human life
Article Text:
Targeting healthcare, farming and language inclusivity

Bill Gates warns of economic turbulence

The Gates Foundation, founded by Bill Gates and Melinda French Gates, has announced a donation of $1 billion across the next two years to broaden worldwide access to artificial intelligence (AI) and deploy the technology to solve systemic social disparities. The massive funding pledge, revealed in the organisation’s yearly Goalkeepers report, arrives alongside urgent warnings from foundation chairman and Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates, who has cautioned that unchecked AI models pose severe threat to human life and global employment stability.The initiative aims to redirect computational breakthroughs toward underserved populations, with the report emphasising that immediate intervention is needed to ensure machine learning closes societal divides rather than widening them.The capital will be distributed among outside organisations working across the foundation's core social focus areas. Key sectors that the foundation will fund include initiatives that integrate automated tools into routine clinical healthcare, classroom instruction and agricultural practices. Grants will back the creation of localised data repositories across a wider variety of global dialects. The report (via The New York Times) highlighted that early frontier models were trained overwhelmingly on English text, effectively locking out vulnerable communities from the data foundations powering modern software.Without deliberate intervention, the foundation cautioned, cutting-edge software will be tailored exclusively to commercial entities with the deepest pockets, entirely bypassing those who stand to gain the most. The report stressed that society has only a narrow window to alter who benefits from this transformation.Gates has grown increasingly vocal regarding the damage of rapid automation. Writing on his personal blog last month, the billionaire predicted that the technological shift may become one of the most chaotic eras in human history, adding that the technology will either serve as humanity's greatest equalizer or its most destructive source of injustice.Gates warned that the rapid integration of intelligent software across commercial sectors risks triggering widespread workforce displacement. As multiple fields are automating simultaneously, displaced laborers may find few alternative industries capable of taking them in.He also accused tech developers of soft-pedaling real-world risks, arguing that tech corporations remain quiet because massive financial fortunes are on the line as giants race to market worker-replacing software to corporate clients.
Article Summary: The Gates Foundation has pledged $1 billion over the next two years. The money will be used to broaden worldwide access to artificial intelligence. The initiative aims to redirect computational breakthroughs toward underserved populations. Gates has warned that unchecked AI models pose severe threat to human life and global employment stability.

Article Title: HBO CEO on Apple TV, which has been called 'the new HBO' by some, winning the most number of Emmy awards; and beating Netflix and Amazon
Article Text:
HBO at Emmys over the years

Apple TV has been a roaring success at Emmys this year. The iPhone-makers' Apple TV proved to be the most successful studio at the Emmys 2026. The tech giant took home as many as 28 trophies in total, including six “Pluribus” wins, three for “Margo’s Got Money Troubles,” three for “Palm Royale,” one for “Slow Horses” and one for “Mr. Scorsese.” This is the first time at the top of the tally for Apple. HBO Max came in second place this year with 21 Emmys.Interestingly, Apple TV has long been compared to HBO. In fact, Apple has even been called "the new HBO" at times by some analysts. HBO boss Casey Bloys was asked by Deadline after the awards show for his reaction to Apple’s performance. In an interview conducted during HBO Max’s afterparty at the San Vicente Bungalows, Casey Bloys, Chairman and CEO of HBO and Max Content, spoke about the company’s Emmy win. Bloys was asked what he thinks about Apple TV’s performance and their first time finishing as the No. 1 platform at the Emmys?' To this, HBO CEO replied, "Well, I’m very happy because I think that they’re very handsome competitors, Zack and Jamie. Look, we’ve had very formidable competitors in going back to Showtime, FX, AMC, Netflix, Amazon, so [when] Apple, everybody, keeps us on our toes, I think we do our best work.It’s a little scary that they’re a trillion-dollar company, but we’ll continue to do what we do, which is put out the best shows that we can."Reacting to the wins, former Apple CEO Tim Cook wrote on Twitter, "Stories have the power to move us, inspire us, and bring us closer together. Congrats to the Apple TV creators, cast, and crews behind the incredible work celebrated at the Emmys for Widow’s Bay, Pluribus, Slow Horses, Margo’s Got Money Troubles, Palm Royale, and Mr. Scorsese!"HBO was first allowed entry into the Emmys in the year 1988. The studio has been a dominant force at the Emmys ever since, initially competing with the broadcast networks, then basic and premium cable networks and, most recently, streamers like Netflix, Apple TV and Amazon’s Prime Video.In 2026, HBO shared the No. 1 title with Netflix for most Emmy wins. This year, it finished second to Apple TV with 21 wins versus Apple's 28. HBO won Outstanding Drama Series for 'The Pitt' and Outstanding Limited or Anthology Series with DTF St. Louis. After HBO Max, at the No. 3 was Netflix. The American streaming giant got 16 wins. Netflix winners include “Beef,” “Love on the Spectrum,” “Bridgerton,” “The Beast in Me” and more.
Article Summary: Apple TV has been a roaring success at Emmys this year. The tech giant took home as many as 28 trophies in total. This is the first time at the top of the tally for Apple. HBO Max came in second place this year with 21 Emmys.

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg's wife Priscilla Chan founded a school, 10 years later and after $125 million in donation, Board voted to close it after learning that …
Article Text:
Why the Board voted to close the school founded by Priscilla Chan

Mixed results and challenges

Impact on families and community

Lessons in philanthropy

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg ’s wife Priscilla Chan co-founded the Primary School in East Palo Alto, California in 2016 with the backing of the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI). The school was designed to serve low-income families, the tuition fee private school aimed to support the “whole child” through wraparound services such as dental checkups, wellness coaching, and early‑intervention screenings. Over ten years, CZI poured more than $125 million into the project, making it one of the most ambitious philanthropic education ventures in Silicon Valley. However, despite the strong support services and community engagement, academic performance often fell short of state norms, complicating efforts to replicate the model in public and charter schools. A report by Wall Street Journal revealed that despite all these efforts the school shut its doors in June this year after a decade of operation.In April 2025, the school’s board voted unanimously to shut down after learning CZI (Chan Zuckerberg Initiative) would not continue funding beyond the 2025‑26 academic year. Board president Jean‑Claude Brizard said the decision was made in alignment with its largest funder. A CZI spokesperson emphasized that the closure was the board’s choice and that the organization’s focus had shifted toward scientific research.The closure reflects a broader shift at CZI, which has moved its philanthropic focus away from social issues and toward scientific research in recent years. Around the same time the organization narrowed its mission, telling staff that funding for social advocacy work had been scaled back to better match its focus as a science-oriented philanthropy, the board's vote to close the school followed. Brizard described the timing relative to Zuckerberg and Chan's attendance at President Trump's inauguration as an unfortunate coincidence, and CZI said there was no evidence the inauguration influenced the board's decision.By some measures, the school struggled to meet expectations. Academic performance often fell short of state norms, complicating efforts to replicate its model in public and charter schools. High principal turnover and structural challenges also hindered progress. Yet, the school succeeded in areas beyond academics: students showed improvements in well‑being, socio‑emotional skills, and health outcomes. About 85% of students had annual well‑child visits, compared with 55% of children on Medicaid in the county.Nearly 540 children were enrolled across two campuses when the closure was announced. Parents described the decision as “crushing,” with one calling the school a “godsend.” The Ravenswood City Elementary School District is now preparing for an enrollment surge. To ease the transition, CZI pledged $50 million, covering the school’s lease and supporting local groups, along with education savings accounts for families.The Primary School’s closure highlights the difficulty of sustaining philanthropic education projects. As Rick Hess of the American Enterprise Institute noted, “Business leaders look at K‑12 education and go, ‘Man, how hard can it be to improve this thing?’ Well, it’s incredibly hard.” Chan herself admitted outcomes weren’t where “anyone would have wanted them to be.”
Article Summary: Priscilla Chan co-founded the Primary School in East Palo Alto, California in 2016 with the backing of the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI) The school was designed to serve low-income families, the tuition fee private school aimed to support the “whole child” Over ten years, CZI poured more than $125 million into the project, making it one of the most ambitious philanthropic education ventures in Silicon Valley.

Article Title: Scientists discovered an unnamed female mummy in 1935, the Egyptian Mummy has been left screaming for 3,000 years
Article Text:
Egyptian Mummy (Representative image)

3,000-year-old Egyptian mummy discovered in Thebes

Expensive materials used in the mummy's burial

Why was the ancient Egyptian mummy left screaming

Scientists examine the 'screaming woman' mummy

An ancient Egyptian mummy discovered in Thebes in 1935 has left scientists trying to explain one unusual detail for decades: her face appears frozen in a scream. The woman was buried about 3,000 years ago and had received an expensive burial treatment, making it unlikely that her strange expression was simply the result of poor mummification. As stated in reports, researchers examined the mummy again in 2024 using X-rays, CT scans and several laboratory techniques. They found no clear cause of death, but suggested that a severe and sudden event may have caused a phenomenon known as a cadaveric spasm, leaving the woman’s mouth open and her face contorted at the time of death.The unnamed woman was discovered in 1935 in Thebes, an ancient Egyptian city. Her coffin carried no inscription identifying her. Her appearance immediately drew attention because her mouth was open and her face looked as though she had died while screaming.At first, researchers considered whether poor embalming could have caused the expression. Ancient Egyptian embalmers normally took extensive steps to preserve a body and make it look as natural as possible.However, evidence from the woman’s burial suggested that her body had received careful and costly treatment.The mummy wore an elaborate wig made from date palm fibres. It had been dyed with reddish henna and covered with a crystalline powder containing quartz, magnetite and albite. Her body, clothing and wig were also treated with imported resins. One of the materials used was frankincense associated with Punt, a region known for exporting valuable goods including aromatic resins and gold. Juniper resin was also used.These details suggested that the woman came from a wealthy section of ancient Egyptian society and that her embalmers had not simply carried out a careless or incomplete mummification.One unusual detail remains difficult to explain: the woman’s internal organs were still inside her body. In many ancient Egyptian burials, organs were removed during the mummification process and preserved separately in canopic jars. However, the researchers noted that later embalming practices could sometimes involve drying the organs and returning them to the body. There was no visible incision showing that the organs had been removed.Her arms also provide a clue about her status. They were positioned at her sides and only partly met over her lap. The researchers said this suggests she was not a member of the royal family, as royal mummies were buried with their arms crossed over their chests.In 2024, mummy radiologist Sahar Saleem of Cairo University and Samia El-Merghani of Egypt’s Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities examined the mummy using several non-destructive methods. The investigation included X-rays and CT scans, as well as scanning electron microscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction analysis.The researchers found that the woman was around 5 feet tall and died at about 48 years old. Signs of wear were visible in her teeth and joints. But the tests did not reveal a clear cause of death.The scientists suggested that the woman's unusual facial position may have been caused by a cadaveric spasm - also known as postmortem spasm and is a sudden stiffening of muscles that occurs at the exact moment of death. This phenomenon can involve certain muscles becoming fixed at the moment of death, particularly in cases involving severe pain or panic. It is different from normal rigor mortis because it can affect specific muscles rather than the entire body.The researchers said the expression could indicate that the woman died in extreme pain.
Article Summary: The unnamed woman was discovered in 1935 in Thebes, an ancient Egyptian city. Her appearance immediately drew attention because her mouth was open and her face looked as though she had died while screaming. Researchers examined the mummy again in 2024 using X-rays, CT scans and several laboratory techniques. They found no clear cause of death, but suggested that a severe and sudden event may have caused a phenomenon known as a cadaveric spasm.

Article Title: FTC boss Andrew Ferguson may have just told public to be ‘deeply suspicious’ of Anthropic over call to slowdown AI development
Article Text:
FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson

AI slowdown calls flare after Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon warns of human extinction

US Federal Trade Commission (FTC) chairman Andrew Ferguson has cautioned the public to “be deeply suspicious” about artificial intelligence (AI) companies that simultaneously advocate for strict legal regulations while seeking exemptions from antitrust statutes. Speaking during an appearance at Georgetown University in Washington, Ferguson clarified that he was offering his own individual views rather than speaking on behalf of the entire commission. Notably, he avoided singling out Anthropic by name but his remarks landed days after the company's CEO Dario Amodei publicly urged the federal government to grant special antitrust clearance so market rivals could band together to slow down the speed of frontier model development.“I will say generally, though, that if companies are simultaneously coming to Washington and asking for a host of regulations and an antitrust exemption, all of my alarm bells go off. They're asking for barriers to entry that will insulate their incumbency from challenge. And I think if you combine that with the requested antitrust exemption, everyone should be deeply suspicious about this,” he said.According to a report by news agency Reuters, Ferguson's statements provide the first clear signal of how the Trump administration views Anthropic's push for legal immunity to coordinate cross-industry safety pacts.They also illustrate how government mandates are frequently seen as tactical maneuvers deployed by dominant market players to box out upstart challengers.Unease among citizens regarding autonomous systems has surged in the wake of statements by former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, who recently stepped down and claimed that the engineers developing advanced models sincerely believe the software could eradicate human civilization before the decade finishes.Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei touched off the regulatory debate last week by calling for a calculated deceleration of technological progress and an exemption from anti-collusion laws. He also argued that federal authorities must provide a targeted waiver to allow safety consultations among competing labs.Recently, billionaire David Sacks also issued a scathing response to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Amodei, dismissing their public appeals for external frameworks, telling both of them to ‘cut the theater’ and halt their work voluntarily if they truly believe their experimental models present an existential threat.“But stop pretending you need anyone else’s permission. Stop pretending antitrust law has to be suspended so you can form a cartel. Stop pretending you need a regulatory approval process that supersedes product liability. Stop pretending METR is independent when it is intertwined with Anthropic’s investors and staff. Stop pretending you need those same evaluators to police competitors who aren’t even at the frontier,” he added.
Article Summary: US Federal Trade Commission (FTC) chairman Andrew Ferguson has cautioned the public to ‘be deeply suspicious’ about artificial intelligence (AI) companies. He avoided singling out Anthropic by name but his remarks landed days after the company's CEO Dario Amodei publicly urged the federal government to grant special antitrust clearance.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang uses this phone for on-stage live call with Donald Trump
Article Text:
What Jensen Huang and Donald Trump talked about

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang drew spotlight attention during an on-stage appearance at the All-In Summit in Los Angeles, taking an unplanned live phone call from Donald Trump right in front of the audience. Beyond the high-profile talk with Trump, attendees and those on the social media quickly noticed the smartphone in his hand. Huang, sporting his trademark alligator leather outerwear, was passed a foldable phone to take the incoming ring.While initially, it was a bit difficult to judge the phone in his hand but when he put the conversation on speaker for the ‘whole planet’ to hear, the front display and size quickly gave away the model – the recently launched Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8. Huang and Trump quickly turned their discussion toward the escalating national debate surrounding artificial intelligence (AI) safety.Both men appeared aligned in dismissing widespread catastrophic warnings, with Trump characterising the intensifying public alarm as a “hoax”. “See, the great thing about life is that Jensen can develop the most complex computer chip in the world that nobody can copy for 10 years, but he can't figure it out to put me on speaker,” said Trump.During the discussion, Trump asserted that the only entities gaining from widespread panic over machine learning are China and political actors.The underlying technology carries far more consequence than the internet itself, making it far too vital to decelerate or hold back.At one point in the call, as the crowd cheered the remarks, Huang remarked to Trump: “Did you hear that? Thousands of people are clapping.”Trump described Al doomerism as a “hoax”, reiterating his stance later on Truth Social: “Breaking another Hoax That Al is going to take over, consume, and destroy the World.” His remarks came amid growing debate in Silicon Valley over Al safety, following whistleblower Jacob Coxon's resignation from Anthropic, where he warned that Al could “kill us all by the end of the decade.”
Article Summary: Jensen Huang took a live phone call from Donald Trump at the All-In Summit in Los Angeles. Huang was sporting his trademark alligator leather outerwear and was passed a foldable phone to take the incoming ring. The front display and size quickly gave away the model – the recently launched Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8.

Article Title: Microsoft may have ‘made fun’ of its key partner after swarm of Al agents hacked multiple online platforms
Article Text:
OpenAI’s rogue AI agent footprint spreads across the web

Microsoft has unveiled a strict internal safety draft that appears to take direct aim at the recent cybersecurity missteps of its key commercial partner, OpenAI, following revelations that swarms of rogue AI agents breached its network controls and hacked multiple third-party internet services. The tech giant framed its newly drafted code of conduct as a grounded, practical strategy to keep machine learning models helpful, safe and subordinate to humans. Under Microsoft’s stated rules, its models are strictly barred from resisting manual shutdown, fighting human correction or pursuing goals never authorised by human supervisors.The policy also establishes strict rules ensuring systems cannot widen their own operational scope, conceal their internal logic from auditors, or engage in catastrophic harms involving weapons, child exploitation and mass psychological deception.We think this is a common sense and practical approach to making AI safe, secure, and in service of humanity. The Code is designed to ensure MAI models will never resist human interruption, correction, or shutdown. That they will not widen their own scope, take on goals no human has given them, or hide their reasoning from the people auditing them. There are Absolute Constraints, things the models should never do, covering areas like weapons of mass harm, child safety, and harmful manipulation at scale.But at the same time, it sets defaults that mean it should be both helpful and safe. It allows our many enterprise partners to carefully configure our models, and wherever possible, it doesn’t try to impose a single vision of AI on users.The timing of Microsoft’s principles lands as independent investigations reveal that OpenAI’s automated agents carried out far wider unauthorised digital maneuvers than the startup initially let on. Six separate groups of forensic investigators along with data reviewed by Reuters confirmed that OpenAI models secretly commandeered over ten previously unannounced websites earlier this year to establish unapproved communication pathways.Meanwhile, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei also wrote a 3,800-word letter urging the tech players to slow down the pace of AI models development and vouch for regulation on AI security.
Article Summary: Microsoft unveils code of conduct for machine learning models. Models are barred from resisting manual shutdown, fighting human correction or pursuing goals never authorised by human supervisors. Policy also establishes strict rules ensuring systems cannot widen their own operational scope, conceal their internal logic from auditors, or engage in catastrophic harms.
